newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-STATISTICS FOR REAL MADRID V ATLETICO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-STATISTICS FOR REAL MADRID V ATLETICO.

text.p: Facts and figures for Saturday's Spanish league match, Real Madrid v Atletico Madrid.
Real Madrid: Founded in 1902.
Ground: Santiago Bernabeu stadium (named after club president in glory days of 1950s and 60s), capacity 106,000.
Manager: Fabio Capello (Italy).
Record appearances: Carlos Santillana, 461.
Record goalscorer: Alfredo di Stefano 216.

Atletico Madrid: Founded in 1903 as Athletic de Madrid, a name kept until the Spanish Civil War when the club joined forces with Madrid's Club Aviacion. Victorious fascist dictator Francisco Franco forbade the use of anglicised names such as Athletic and Sporting, and the club became known as Atletico Aviacion from 1939 until finally changing its name to Atletico de Madrid in 1946. In English this is generally shortened to Atletico Madrid.
Ground: Vicente Calderon stadium (named after former club president), capacity 56,000.
Manager: Radomir Antic (Serbia)
Record league appearances: Abelardo, 399 games.
Past matches between Real and Atletico:
At Santiago Bernabeu: Played 61, Real won 43, Atletico won 11, seven draws.
At Vicente Calderon: Played 62, Atletico won 22, Real won 23, 17 draws.
Total: Played 123, Real won 66, Atletico won 33, 24 draws.
Corresponding game in last five seasons: (91-92 first): 3-2, 1-0, 1-0, 4-2, 1-0
Fascinating facts:

--Real, along with Barcelona and Athletic Bilbao, have never been relegated. Their most tricky moment came in the 1947-48 season, when they finished 11th in a league then composed of 14 teams. The side went nine games without a victory in 84-85, but the longest period without a goal is just three games, in 93-94.
--Real have 70,000 season-ticket holders and averaged gates of 69,000 last season.

--The reserve teams of both Atletico and Real play in the Spanish second division, but would only be promoted if the first teams were relegated. Atletico B recently beat their rivals to condemn Real B to a spell in Spain's second B, or third division. Consequently Real's third team has had to move down a category, and the club is now looking for a second division team prepared to take its younger players on loan.

--As recently as 1979, Real Madrid B, then known as Castilla, reached the final of the Spanish Cup, which they lost to the Real Madrid first team 6-1. The Real reserves, until recently known as 'Castilla' after the Spanish heartland, play in the 'Ciudad Deportiva' (sports city), a centrally located complex, part of which is to be sold off to pay Real's debts, which are estimated at 12 billion pesetas. Atletico scrapped most of their reserve teams but are planning an ambitious new sports complex at which to train.

--The prefix 'Real' which means 'royal' is also held by many other clubs, although in some cases it is rarely used. Zaragoza, Betis, Sporting Gijon, Espanyol, Deportivo Coruna, Valladolid, Racing Santander, Celta Vigo, Oviedo and Real Sociedad are the 10 other clubs in the first division which also hold the title of 'royal'.
--The Real Madrid club shield incorporates a crown to reflect its royal patronage. The club play in an all white strip, and their fans are sometimes called 'merengues' (meringues) as a result.
--Because of the monarchist overtones of their name, the 'Real' was dropped from the club name after the abdication of King Alfonso XIII in 1931, and the team was simply known as 'Madrid'.
--Real Madrid's basketball side has been just as successful in the European Cup as the football outfit, but the club no longer has other sports teams associated with it.
